title: The Importance of Speech Genre for End-of-Turn Detector Training
abstract: arXiv:2610.39742v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: End-of-turn (EoT) detection has been studied mostly through features, models, and modalities, while the speech genre of the training data has drawn far less attention. We isolate this factor. Using one reproducible annotation pipeline, we build a matched pair of corpora, multi-turn human-human conversational and single-turn human-machine, and train the same streaming ConvLSTM EoT detector on each. Across four test sets the conversational model reaches up to +0.45 higher F1, driven by fewer false alarms on the mid-turn pauses and hesitations that are rare in single-turn corpora. This conversational-training effect is not specific to frame-level decoding. Under a matched complete-or-not test it also appears at the utterance level, across two encoders, but only on conversational test data. Testing only on single-turn speech, as most prior work does, therefore hides the benefit of conversational training data. Against open-source baselines

translated_title: 语音体裁对轮次结束检测器训练的重要性
translated_abstract: 轮次结束检测的研究大多集中在特征、模型和模态上，而训练数据的语音体裁却很少受到关注。我们单独分离出这一因素进行研究。使用一套可复现的标注流程，我们构建了一组匹配的语料库对——多轮人人会话语料和单轮人机交互语料，并在每个语料库上训练相同的流式ConvLSTM轮次结束检测器。在四个测试集上，会话式模型取得了高达+0.45的更高F1分数，这主要源于在轮次中途停顿和犹豫上误报的减少，而这些停顿和犹豫在单轮语料库中很少出现。这种会话式训练效果并非仅限于帧级解码：在一项匹配的“完整与否”测试中，该效果在话语层面、跨两种编码器同样显现，但仅在会话式测试数据上体现。因此，像大多数先前工作那样仅在单轮语音上测试，会掩盖会话式训练数据的优势。
tldr: 该论文通过构建匹配的多轮人人会话与单轮人机语料库进行对照实验，发现使用会话式数据训练的轮次结束检测器因能更好地识别轮次中途的停顿和犹豫而获得更高F1分数，而仅在单轮语音上评估会掩盖会话式训练数据的优势。
